reason: The filter picture shows blood entering the kidney filter and small substances crossing it, so this starts the filtration goal.
expectation: The filter should let water and other small substances through while keeping blood cells and large proteins in the vessels.

alternatives.reason: The ureters could be fitted first, but I want to follow filtration and recovery first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose and salts through along with wastes, so the filtered fluid needs the recovery tube next.
reaction: It is interesting that the filter does not separate out just the waste.
reason: The recovery tube picture shows useful substances returning from the fluid to the blood.
expectation: Glucose, some salts and much of the water should return to the blood, leaving fluid containing wastes.

effect: The recovery tube returned useful substances and much water to the blood, leaving urine. The remaining goal is to connect the kidneys to the bladder.
reaction: It makes sense that filtering is followed by taking useful materials back.
reason: The ureters are shown leading from the kidneys toward the bladder, and the urinary system has a slot for them.
expectation: The ureters should connect to the kidneys in the urinary system model.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also has a slot, but I chose to build the route from the kidneys downward.

effect: The ureters now lead from the kidneys toward the empty bladder position.
reaction: The muscular squeezes explain how the tubes move urine along.
reason: The bladder fits the remaining slot and completes the route from the kidneys.
expectation: The bladder should connect to the ureters as a place to hold urine.

effect: The bladder completes the continuous route from both kidneys, and urine remains the same fluid as it travels into the bladder. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The completed route is clear, though fitting the bladder was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering blood and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidney does more than simply remove waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was the least interesting step because its position and purpose were already clear, although it completed the model.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and salts pass through the filter along with wastes and have to be recovered.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; the pictures and slots explained both the filtering sequence and the route to the bladder.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because following a familiar organ through filtering, recovery and drainage made its job easier to picture, even though the final fittings were predictable.
